# E1-final — the headline three-way comparison in the final version

*Generated by `agent/tools/campaign.py reports` from `results/campaign.json` and the experiment record (`agent/THESIS_EXPERIMENTS.md`). Edit those, then regenerate — not this file.*

**Status:** running

## The question

On TSVC class R (with class A and D controls), prompt version 3, the fixed DiscoPoP, packaging v4: DiscoPoP alone vs the Haiku agent vs Haiku, Sonnet, Opus and Fable alone — who ships correct, race-free, faster programs, and who ships unusable ones?

## What is in this folder

- [`runs/`](runs/) — 11 archived run(s): the evidence
- [`preflight/`](preflight/) — 2 smoke run(s) before the launch

## From the experiment record (§7 run log)

### `e1f_smoke` — 2026-10-02, server, **E1-final smoke (configuration check, not counted)** (12 trials)

- **Setup.** `tsvc_b1/s211` (class R) and `tsvc_b1/s000` (class A) × 1: job 1 on node 0 — `default_v3`, `discopop_gate_v3`, `bare_llm_v3` with Haiku (20:14 → 20:40 UTC); job 2 on node 1 at the same time on the same new run id — `bare_llm_v3` with Sonnet 5, Opus 5.5, Fable 5.1 (20:15 → 20:25). Commit `b56a086a`, PARITY OK; both sweeps clean.
- **Result.** Every arm and model runs end to end: prompt version 3 in every agent command, the speed check ON in the agent and DiscoPoP-alone arms (`speed_check_off` false everywhere), 0 failed model calls. Outcomes (not counted): `s211` — agent FASTER (5 calls, 12.6 min), DiscoPoP alone no-change, Haiku alone does not compile (`private(i)` on an undeclared `i`), Sonnet, Opus, Fable alone FASTER; `s000` — FASTER in all six. **The profiling lock worked live:** the two jobs profiled each loop once between them (job 1 `s211`, job 2 `s000`; the same `profile_sha256` in both logs). Time per trial: the agent 5–13 min, a model alone 0.3–2 min plus verification (~1.7 min wall).
- **What it decides.** The configuration is right; the main runs go ahead as pre-registered (§6, 2 Oct). Archived in `results/E01f_final_three_way/preflight/e1f_smoke/`.

| Date | Repo | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-02 | plan | **E1-final pre-registered — written before any main trial (the smoke `e1f_smoke` is a configuration check, never counted).** **Runs** (registered in `results/campaign.json`, group E1-final): the agent and DiscoPoP alone (`default_v3`, `discopop_gate_v3`, Haiku) on class R × 5 in four runs on the four 12-core lanes with E1c's split — `e1f_r_1` (s112 s121 s1213 s127 s211), `e1f_r_2` (s212 s241 s243 s244 s252), `e1f_r_3` (s254 s255 s281 s291), `e1f_r_4` (s292 s293 s331 s341) — then `e1f_a` (class A × 1) and `e1f_d` (class D × 3); the model alone (`bare_llm_v3`) in ONE RUN PER MODEL, so each model's read-out selects its own run: `e1f_bare_haiku` (`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`), `e1f_bare_sonnet` (`claude-sonnet-5`), `e1f_bare_opus` (`claude-opus-5-5`), `e1f_bare_fable` (`claude-fable-5-1`), each class R × 5, A × 1, D × 3 (jobs split by class and by `--reps` over lanes; Opus and Fable never at the same time). Threads 6,12, repeats 5, speed check ON, sizes from `t0_1_e1f_sizes`; one commit for every run. **Outcomes per trial** (as E1c): race-free FASTER against the sequential original; unusable (BROKEN, racy, slower, not compiling). A model-alone parallel program is race-free only where `race_check.py` finds it clean (run on every model-alone parallel program of all four models). **Tests, class R, paired by loop over the 18 loops** (`main_comparison_stats.py e1f_r_1..4:default_v3+discopop_gate_v3 e1f_bare_<model>:bare_llm_v3 --three-way default_v3 --bare bare_llm_v3 --baseline-arm discopop_gate_v3 --races …`, once per model): (T1, H1) the agent against DiscoPoP alone — Wilcoxon signed-rank on per-loop medians, one-sided, Cliff's delta, bootstrap interval of the median ratio; (T2–T5, H13) the agent against each model alone — per-loop unusable rate, Wilcoxon one-sided (the agent fewer); (T6–T9, reach) the agent against each model alone — per-loop race-free FASTER rate, Wilcoxon one-sided (the agent more). Holm over T1–T9 inside E1-final; reported also in the campaign family (M = 31 + 9 = 40). (H2) the agent's unusable programs: a count with every case named, no p-value — expected 0. **Controls, descriptive:** class A — the agent's speed-up ÷ DiscoPoP alone's per loop (no harm if ≥ 0.9); class D — every valid trial declines. **Exclusions, fixed now:** a harness edit (SCAFFOLD_MODIFIED) is its own row, never counted, the trial repeated once; a trial whose model call failed (`llm_call_failures`) is re-run, never counted; nothing else is dropped. **Expectations** (from E1c-v3.1: agent 71/90, Haiku alone 39/90 with 46 unusable): T1 rejected; H2 holds; T2–T5 rejected for every model; T6–T9 rejected against Haiku alone, open against Opus and Fable (E12: the strong models alone match the agent on real loops). **What decides what:** a strong model alone that reaches as far as the agent with fewer or equal unusable programs is reported as such — the thesis claim then narrows to "a small model with DiscoPoP matches a strong model alone at a fraction of the cost" (cost per trial reported for every arm and model: model calls, tokens, time). Secondary, descriptive: E1-final against E1c-v3.1 per loop (`E1-final-vs-E1c`) | Plan, pre-registered |
| 2026-10-03 | decision | **Harness edits are prevented and redone, never just left out (the author: "i do not like that at all … we need to either avoid that in the first place not just by telling the model not to do it … or fix it then redo the trial; just no counting is not a good idea"). Fix 103, built and verified before any trial it governs.** Until now a program that edited the lines the harness measures with (`SCAFFOLD_MODIFIED`: the `#include`, `pb_mix(nl)`, `PB_MAIN`, in older packages the timer and digest) was reported in its own row and left out of every rate (the author, 24 Sep); only the agent enforced the lines (Fix 97, its gate's stage `harness`, retry not charged), the twins and the model alone had nothing but the instruction (E12: Fable 5.1 alone wrote a parallel path and a serial fallback, each with its own `pb_mix(nl)`, in 3 of 10 ORDER-2 trials). **(1) Prevention in the arms without the agent's gate** (`discopop_agent/gate/harness_guard.py`, used by `bare_llm.py` and `twin.py`): after the model's turn the finished file is checked with the JUDGE's own rules (`gate/scaffold.py`, a byte-identical copy of `agent/tools/scaffold.py`, kept identical by `test_scaffold.py`); a violation is sent back in the agent's own words (Fix 97's stage-`harness` message — its guidance, `check_protected`'s diagnostic, its retry instruction; the feature check `harness-guard` proves them verbatim) in the SAME model session, at most 2 re-asks, never charged as an attempt; if the lines are still edited the edit is discarded and the file stays as it was — as the agent's gate never keeps a candidate it refused. Recorded per trial: `harness_reasks`, `harness_discards`; every re-ask is a model call in `llm_calls` and the token log. A turn that leaves the measurement alone is unchanged (the check runs after it and says nothing; the first call keeps its session so it can be resumed, model-facing identical — a fresh session either way); prompt manifest: no arm's text changed. **(2) Backstop in the runner** (`cli.py`, `HARNESS_EDIT_REDOS = 2`): a trial the harness still classifies `SCAFFOLD_MODIFIED` is redone automatically, at most twice; every attempt is kept under `<run>/_harness_edit/<benchmark>/<arm>/<model>/rep<N>/attempt<K>/` (outside `benchmarks/`, so no tool counts it) and listed in the trial's `harness_edit_redos`. **(3) Counting:** a trial that still edits the measurement after both redos COUNTS — in the denominator, as unusable (`main_comparison_stats`: `measurement_kept_edited`; `e2b1_stats`: bucket `measurement-edited`, unsafe). Trials from before 3 Oct (no `harness_edit_redos`) keep the rule they were registered with. **(4) The agent's own harness stage gets the judge's rules too** (`gate/harness_lines.check_protected` now also runs `scaffold.check`; `phase_a.py` unchanged): while this was built, E1-final's agent arm shipped a harness edit Fix 97 could not see — `s331` rep4 peeled the last repetition and added `pb_mix(R - 1);`, no protected line changed. Over every archived trial the combined check flags exactly the 16 recorded harness edits (all arms, packaging v3 and v4) and nothing else. **Inertness on E1-final's agent runs, measured:** every candidate the agent's model writes in E1-final is scanned for what the new rule adds (a new `pb_*` line that the old rule let through; `fix103_scan`, run when the agent runs end, over `e1f_r_1`–`4`, `e1f_a`, `e1f_d`). At 03:00 (67 agent trials, 416 candidates) one trial is affected — `s331` rep4, the shipped edit (`s331` rep1's such candidate was already refused by Fix 97 with the same message: unchanged). Every affected trial is set aside on the server (`<run>/_superseded_fix103/`) and redone on the fixed agent in run `e1f_fix103_redo`, from a copy of its own run's DiscoPoP profile (the same draw as its sister trials); every other agent trial stands as run — the new rule says nothing in it. The final scan's numbers go to §7. Verified: feature checks `harness-guard` (new: the Fable case fixed on one re-ask in the same session; an unfixed edit discarded after 3 calls; a clean edit untouched; the twin re-asked on a profiled program), `harness-lines`, `bare-llm`, `twin-run`, `twin-prompt` and the prompt checks; `test_integrity.py` (the redo through the real run loop: once → 2 attempts, always → 3 attempts, counted), `test_scaffold.py`, `test_arms.py`, `test_prompt_v2.py`; mypy clean; `prompt_manifest.py diff`: no arm's text changed. **E1-final deviation (recorded before its model-alone runs):** the agent and DiscoPoP-alone runs (`e1f_r_1`–`4`, and `e1f_a`, `e1f_d` launched on the same commit `912e3d9b` while lanes were idle) run without (2); none of them has shown a harness edit so far, and any that does is redone with the fixed runner. The model-alone runs (`e1f_bare_*`) run on the fixed commit. The pre-registered "harness edit: own row, repeated once" is replaced by (2)–(3) for every E1-final trial. **E12:** Fable's 3 harness-edit trials are redone on the fixed commit (next row) | Decision (author), Fix 103 |
